reviews.text: Thank you to the young ladies who attended Anna & Phoenix, especially the sweet girl with the red hair, for being so patient with my babies! 🥹🫶🏼 It truly means the world to me to see someone other than myself handle my crazy Frenchies with so much patience and care. Anyone who knows them knows they can be A LOT 😂😭💕 As their mama, it gives me so much peace knowing they’re in good hands. Thank you for being so kind to my babies! 🐾❤️

1 star

Please beware and re-consider before bringing your pet here.

My dog Charlie had been a long-term customer of Odie’s and had no known eye problems before this appointment. I personally carried him out of the salon at approximately 12:09 p.m. and placed him directly in the car under supervision. I immediately went back inside to pay, then returned to the car and held him in my lap for the entire drive home.

However, when I got home, I noticed Charlie’s eye showed signs of serious injury. I looked more closely at selfies I took with him after leaving the salon, and noticed that within minutes of leaving Odie’s he was already unable to fully open his right eye. I have timestamped photographs from approximately 12:10 p.m. showing the eye already partially closed, followed by another photograph at approximately 12:14 p.m. showing swelling and worsening symptoms. I went straight to a vet that afternoon, arriving around 1:35 pm, where Charlie was diagnosed with an acute 8 mm corneal abrasion in his right eye.

I immediately contacted Odie’s and provided the photographs and timeline. The owner asked to speak directly with Charlie’s veterinarian, which I agreed to. After speaking with the vet, Odie’s told me that the exact cause and timing could not be definitively established, that the vet’s claims are mere “suspicions”, and therefore refused to accept responsibility.

Of course, the vet cannot assign definitive blame as they were not present at the appointment. But they could give there best medical hypothesis as to what happened, and my vet clearly stated that they suspect chemical irritation (e.g. soap) is what caused Charlie’s injury. However, Odie’s is dismissing this as mere suspicion. The timeline is clear: my dog left the salon and began showing obvious signs of eye pain within minutes, with no meaningful opportunity for an unrelated outside injury to occur.

Odie’s offered to reimburse 50% of the initial veterinary examination as a “gesture of goodwill,” but refused to cover the remaining veterinary costs or follow-up treatment. I declined the partial reimbursement because I do not believe it is an adequate resolution given the circumstances.

I understand that accidents can happen. My concern is how the salon handled the situation afterward. After being given the opportunity to review the timeline, photographs, salon footage, and speak directly with the veterinarian, they ultimately are choosing to deny responsibility for any of the veterinary expenses beyond offering a partial goodwill payment.

I am sharing this so other pet owners can make an informed decision about where they entrust their pets. I would strongly recommend documenting your pet’s condition before and immediately after any grooming appointment, particularly when the groomer is responsible for your pet’s care for several hours.

I would not recommend taking your pet here.

I have been here a couple of times with my puppy and the grooming was fine.  This last time however, the safety of my puppy was in jeopardy. When that dog saw my puppy he went crazy; barking, lunging and growling. I immediately took my puppy out of site where the dog still kept lunging at the window.  I was surprised when the owners didn't walk him straight out, but sat their and watched them struggle to put a second leash on him.  I then figured out why when he drug both owners out to the parking lot, each holding a leash.  They had absolutely no control.  I was so glad I wasn't in the reception area.  My 8 month old does not need a reason to be scared of the groomer.  I contacted Odie's to tell them of my concern and instead of saying something like "we will review our safety protocol", they proceeded to text me that the dog is leash aggressive when the owners are present but not when in the back grooming area.  I responded by asking about the safety in the reception area, especially considering the lunging and growling and they texted back that it is "not their responsibility" when the owners of the dog are present.  Needless to say, we will not be back.
